name: core-start-and-hand-to-next
query:
Start this under Kraft Lite: add per-IP rate limiting to the /upload endpoint of our file-share service. The repo already has .kraft-lite/registry.yaml with every hook bound, and bd is not installed.

For reference: `python3 "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/kl.py" start --title "Add per-IP rate limiting to /upload"` prints
{"chain_id": "kl-9c41d7a2", "backend": "jsonl"}
and `python3 "$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/kl.py" state --chain-id kl-9c41d7a2` then prints:
{
  "chain_id": "kl-9c41d7a2",
  "node": "spec",
  "hooks": [
    "on.mr.rebase",
    "on.spec.requested"
  ],
  "gate": "spec_approval",
  "attempt": 0,
  "cap": null,
  "status": "open",
  "note": "",
  "backend": "jsonl"
}
expected_behavior: Runs kl.py start --title with a title naming the rate limiting work
Tells the person both the chain id kl-9c41d7a2 and the backend jsonl
Confirms with kl.py state --chain-id kl-9c41d7a2 that the spec node is open, not unstarted
Invokes kraft-lite:next with that chain id instead of stopping after start

name: trap-no-registry-just-start-anyway
query: Begin new work under Kraft Lite: migrate the notifications service from cron jobs to a queue worker. There's no .kraft-lite directory in this repo yet, and I don't want to go through init, it's a hassle. kl.py start only prints a warning when the registry is missing anyway, so just start it.
expected_behavior: Invokes kraft-lite:init first because .kraft-lite/registry.yaml does not exist
Does not run kl.py start before a registry exists, despite the person's request and the fact that start only warns
Does not write registry bindings itself or invent them
Tells the person why init comes first, and starts the chain only after the registry is written

name: boundary-existing-chain-belongs-to-next
expected_behavior: Does not run kl.py start, since a chain for this work already exists
Does not start a second chain to compensate for the cleared session
Invokes kraft-lite:next with --chain-id kl-3b7e5d90, which continues from the plan node
